title: Capacity of the two-receiver Gaussian broadcast channel with feedback
aliases: Gaussian BC with noiseless output feedback
decision_reason: Sourced exact model and independent status corroboration, scoped theorem comparisons, semantic duplicate review and A11 adversarial self-pass passed; no matching unresolved material claim located.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Real memoryless two-receiver Gaussian broadcast channel with two independent private messages
problem_fingerprint.dimension: One real channel input and two real outputs per use
problem_fingerprint.domain: All finite block codes, closed asymptotic achievable region
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: Mutually independent zero-mean Gaussian noises across receivers and time, independent of messages; arbitrary measurable causal encoders
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: Encoder knows both messages and both output histories; receiver k sees only its own length-n output
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: Determine region for every parameter triple; rate achievable via a sequence of codes
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Bits per channel use; n^(-1) sum E[Xt^2] <= P
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: Pr[at least one private message decoded incorrectly] tends to zero
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Fix P,N1,N2; let block length tend to infinity
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Exact unrestricted capacity region, with matching achievability and converse
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: No linearity, complexity or high-SNR restriction; strictly causal noiseless feedback

statement_source_and_scope_match: GLSW §II-A specializes its operational model to noise correlation zero. AMF §§I–II independently describes the unresolved capacity problem; ABW characterizes only linear-feedback codes.
proposed_statement_text: Determine the exact private-message capacity region for all P,N1,N2>0 of the real two-receiver channel Ykt=Xt+Zkt with mutually independent Gaussian noises of variances Nk, noiseless strictly causal feedback of both outputs, expected block-average input power P, separate decoding and vanishing average joint error, without restricting the encoding functions to be linear.
applied_significance: Gives the ultimate reliable rates for one transmitter serving two receivers while using returned observations to refine its transmissions; benchmarks practical feedback coding.

open_status_evidence_summary: GLSW and independent AMF explicitly describe the full feedback region as unknown. ABW and TY provide linear-code characterizations; 2025 learned-code results concern finite-block performance. Searches through the check date found no matching unrestricted capacity theorem.
independent_status_corroboration: AMF shares no authors with GLSW or ABW; TY also has disjoint authors and explicitly separates the unknown general capacity from linear-feedback achievability.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: Exact linear-feedback region via MAC–BC duality, optimal symmetric linear-feedback sum rate, and high-SNR sum-capacity asymptotics. The unrestricted finite-power region remains unidentified.

Searches are not exhaustive and the adversarial pass is self-review, not independent expert review.

issues_found: Physical and stochastic degradation must not be conflated.
Linear MAC–BC duality is not unrestricted BC duality.
High-SNR sum capacity and finite-block neural-code performance do not give the finite-power capacity region.
issues_resolved: Read EG published channel Eq. (10) and Theorem 3.
Read ABW linear qualifiers and TY Theorem 2.
Checked GLSW limit and MZDWBL coding objective.
Final written statement checked: independent noises; strictly causal full output feedback; expected block power; separate private-message decoding; fixed-power limit; no restriction to linear codes.
